sections.heading: What fractions and decimals mean
sections.body:
A **fraction** shows part of a whole, like 3/4. The bottom number, the **denominator**, tells how many **equal** parts the whole is cut into. The top number, the **numerator**, tells how many of those parts you have. A cake is cut into 6 equal slices and you eat 1, so you ate **1/6** of the cake.

A **decimal** shows parts of a whole after a dot called the **decimal point**. The first place after the point is **tenths**. The second place is **hundredths**.

- 0.3 = 3 tenths = 3/10
- 0.25 = 25 hundredths = 25/100, like 25 centavos out of ₱1

Learn these by heart:

| Fraction | Decimal |
| --- | --- |
| 1/2 | 0.5 |
| 1/4 | 0.25 |
| 3/4 | 0.75 |
| 1/10 | 0.1 |

sections.heading: Comparing and simplifying
sections.body:
- **Same bottom:** the bigger top is the bigger fraction. 5/9 is more than 2/9.
- **Same top:** the smaller bottom is the bigger fraction. 1/2 is more than 1/5, because fewer pieces means bigger pieces.
- **Simplify:** divide the top and the bottom by the same number. 10/15, divided by 5, is **2/3**. A fraction is in **simplest form** when no number except 1 divides both.
- **Decimals:** add zeros at the end until they have the same number of digits after the point, then compare. 0.6 = 0.60, which is more than 0.58.

sections.heading: Adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing
sections.body:
- **Same bottom:** add or subtract the tops and keep the bottom. 1/5 + 3/5 = 4/5. 7/9 − 2/9 = 5/9.
- **Decimals:** line up the points. Add zeros if needed. 2.5 + 0.35 → 2.50 + 0.35 = 2.85.
- **A fraction of a number:** divide by the bottom, then multiply by the top. 3/5 of 20: 20 ÷ 5 = 4, then 4 × 3 = 12.
- **Divide by a fraction:** count how many fit. How many 1/2-cup scoops are in 3 cups? Each cup holds 2 scoops, so 3 × 2 = 6.

sections.heading: Common traps
sections.body:
- **Adding the bottoms.** 1/5 + 3/5 is 4/5, not 4/10.
- **Upside down.** The whole goes on the bottom.
- **More digits is not bigger.** 0.45 is less than 0.5.
- **Lining up the last digits.** Line up the decimal points instead.
- **Answering the wrong part.** If 1 of 6 slices is eaten, 5/6 is the part left, not the part eaten.

glossaryTerms.definition: A number that shows part of a whole, written as top/bottom, like 3/4.
glossaryTerms.taglish: Fraction – bahagi ng isang buo, halimbawa 1/6 ng cake kung 1 sa 6 na hiwa ang kinain

glossaryTerms.definition: The top number of a fraction. It tells how many parts you have.
glossaryTerms.taglish: Numerator – ang numero sa itaas; ilang bahagi ang hawak mo

glossaryTerms.definition: The bottom number of a fraction. It tells how many equal parts make the whole.
glossaryTerms.taglish: Denominator – ang numero sa ibaba; ilang pantay na hati ang buo

glossaryTerms.definition: A fraction is in simplest form when no number except 1 divides both its top and its bottom.
glossaryTerms.taglish: Simplest form – pinakasimpleng anyo; wala nang numerong puwedeng mag-divide sa taas at baba maliban sa 1

glossaryTerms.definition: A number with a decimal point, where the digits after the point are parts of a whole, like 0.25.
glossaryTerms.taglish: Decimal – numerong may tuldok, gaya ng 0.25 o 25 sentimo sa ₱1

glossaryTerms.definition: Tenths are the first place after the decimal point (0.3 = 3/10). Hundredths are the second place (0.07 = 7/100).
glossaryTerms.taglish: Tenths at hundredths – una at ikalawang puwesto pagkatapos ng tuldok; ikasampu at ikasandaang bahagi
